rationale: Bcheck deliberately stops tracking a local whose address is passed; the audited value remains rooted by the protected input or output carrier.
The reported child is borrowed from a protected argument, attribute owner, closure, or environment that remains live across the audited call.
The function uses reviewed variable-count or helper-owned protection accounting that exceeds bcheck's stack-depth abstraction and is covered by maacheck and dynamic memory gates.
The fresh value is immediately installed in a protected container or handed to a callee under an audited ownership contract before another allocation can expose it.
The reported object remains reachable through the process-preserved canonical runtime graph authenticated and retained from namespace initialization.
The reported values are stored in an explicitly protected vector, environment, or root carrier before the subsequent allocating operation.
The test-only ALTREP callback deliberately uses caller-balanced protection to create an adversarial collection schedule; it is not shipped production behavior.
